intent: A force quiz with a snap: three bite forces rise to scale so the lion and hippo look small, a white flash marks the clamp of jaws built to close and not to open, and a pin lands on the estuaries of northern Australia where the biggest of them wait for anything that comes to drink.
pacing_profile: question read verbatim, three options, 3-s beat, reveal with the number, story beats shaped per episode (brief.md), punchline + short follow
pause_policy: Pause only at the marked ellipses; the beat is real silence (ticks come from quizscore.py).
title: Which animal has the STRONGEST bite?

lines.direction: the question, cold — curiosity comes from the map moving under it
lines.text: Which animal has the strongest bite?

lines.direction: quick, each option its own beat

lines.text: The saltwater crocodile. The strongest bite ever measured on a living animal: 3,700 pounds per square inch.

lines.direction: ease back over the Top End; three forces rise to scale on 'lion' with the crocodile towering; a hippo sticker on 'hippo'; a muscle sticker on 'half' as the north pulses
lines.text: A lion manages under a third of that. A hippo reaches about half.

lines.direction: hold on the north; a white flash on 'clamp' with the jaws tag; a tooth sticker on 'open'; a band sticker on 'band' as the north pulses
lines.text: The muscles are built to clamp shut, not to open. A rubber band can hold the mouth closed.

lines.direction: tighten on the Kakadu wetlands; a wave sticker on 'rivers'; the Kakadu pin and the 16,460 N card on 'Australia'; a warning sticker on 'drink' as a crocodile sticker lands and the north pulses; the pin leaves at the end
lines.text: The giants live in the rivers and estuaries of northern Australia, longer than a car, and ambush whatever comes to drink.

lines.direction: punchline, then a short follow — the outro visual asks
lines.text: Jaws that never let go. Follow us.
